links.outcome: Reader accuracy, sensitivity and specificity with versus without AI assistance for ovarian mass diagnosis
links.effect: Junior/intermediate radiologists improved with AI (ACC 80.8 vs 75.3, p=0.00015; SEN 79.5 vs 74.6, p=0.029; SPE 81.7 vs 75.8, p=0.0032); GPs with AI reached radiologist-level performance.
links.quote: There was a significant improvement in junior and intermediate radiologists who were assisted by AI compared to those who were not assisted by AI (ACC: 80.8 vs. 75.3, p = 0.00015; SEN: 79.5 vs. 74.6, p = 0.029; SPE: 81.7 vs. 75.8, p = 0.0032).

links.outcome: AI diagnostic performance compared with senior radiologists on the same external video data
links.effect: OvaMTA AUC 0.911 on 159 videos, comparable to senior radiologists (ACC 86.2 vs 88.1, p=0.50; SEN 81.8 vs 88.6, p=0.16; SPE 89.2 vs 87.6, p=0.68).
links.quote: In video-based external testing, OvaMTA recognised 159 videos with ovarian masses with AUC of 0.911, and is comparable to the performance of senior radiologists (ACC: 86.2 vs. 88.1, p = 0.50; SEN: 81.8 vs. 88.6, p = 0.16; SPE: 89.2 vs. 87.6, p = 0.68).

links.outcome: Model performance on internal versus external test cohorts from other hospitals
links.effect: Detection AUC 0.970 internal vs 0.877 external; Dice 0.887 internal vs 0.819 external; diagnosis AUC 0.941 on both internal and external sets.
links.quote: OvaMTA-Seg also performed well in ovarian mass detection from test images, including healthy ovaries and masses (internal test area under the curve [AUC]: 0.970; external test AUC: 0.877).

screen.reason: The study conducts a reader study comparing diagnostic performance of physicians (junior/intermediate radiologists and general practitioners) with versus without AI assistance.
